docs.purpose: Lets someone browse and filter Toronto building permits — by status, trade, cost range, ward or search text — with pagination and each permit's matched trade classifications attached. A special mode on the same endpoint instead returns upcoming committee-of-adjustment approvals that have not yet become a building permit, so users see construction leads before the permit itself exists.
docs.data_story: It reads 4 tables — `permits`, `permit_trades`, `trades` and `coa_applications` and writes nothing. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 1 place: `web_dashboard`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: No SPEC LINK header. Sort column validated against an ALLOWED_SORT allowlist (SQL-injection guard). The source=pre_permits branch delegates to getUpcomingLeads() in src/lib/coa/pre-permits.ts, which queries coa_applications directly rather than permits. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: DISCLOSURE (unauthenticated): `SELECT p.*` (route.ts:139) returns EVERY column of `permits` — 171 columns per docs/specs/00-architecture/01_database_schema.md:70. Named from src/lib/db/generated/schema.ts (permits pgTable) these include `owner`, `builder_name`, `est_const_cost`, `bid_value`, `latitude`, `longitude` (exact permit coordinates), `geo_id`, `postal`, `photo_url`, `lead_id`, `raw_json` (the untouched upstream Toronto Open Data record), plus the whole derived cost/zoning/max-build block (`cost_fb_total`, `cost_coa_total`, `cost_gut_total`, `max_build_fsi`, `coa_fsi`, `opt_*`, …). So an anonymous caller receives owner names, builder names, construction valuations, precise lat/lng and the derived cost-model columns for any permit, with an attacker-controlled `limit` capped at 100 per page and unbounded paging. Toronto building permits are an open-data source, so `owner`/valuation may be public-by-origin — but the DERIVED cost columns are the same proprietary family that /api/parcels/lookup gates behind session + subscription, and `raw_json` is an unreviewed passthrough. Worth an explicit ruling. Second finding: the trade-fetch query keys on `pt.permit_num || '--' || pt.revision_num = ANY($1)` (route.ts:154) — a string-concat join that cannot use a composite index. CHECKLIST agreement: routes-index.json census_reads (permits, permit_trades, trades, coa_applications) matches exactly; coa_applications is reached only via the ?source=pre_permits branch (route.ts:13-18 -> src/lib/coa/pre-permits.ts:126). getUpcomingLeads maps rows through mapCoaToPermitDto (src/lib/coa/pre-permits.ts:152-165) so the CoA response exposes `applicant` as `builder_name` (pre-permits.ts:73). | Caching: none observed — no revalidate/dynamic export and no Cache-Control header in src/app/api/permits/route.ts:1-195 | Pagination: page/limit/offset. limit = Math.min(Number(limit), 100) default 20 (route.ts:58, :126); page = Math.max(1, page) default 1 (route.ts:57, :125); offset = (page-1)*limit (route.ts:127) bound as $n (route.ts:141-142). Upper clamp only — no lower clamp on limit (a negative or NaN limit is not rejected). Response carries {page, limit, total, total_pages} (route.ts:181-186). Pre-permits branch: limit only, Math.min(...,100) default 50 (route.ts:15), pagination hardcoded to one page (route.ts:25). | Other guards / classification: PUBLIC by classification: '/api/permits' is in PUBLIC_PREFIXES (src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:70), matched at route-guard.ts:170 -> 'public'; middleware passes it through at src/middleware.ts:43-45. No AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES entry precedes it. | Locking tests: src/tests/api.infra.test.ts, src/tests/search.logic.test.ts.
